I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed on non-ASCII domain names when the email encoding is non-unicode.

### Cause
When the machine hostname contains non-ASCII characters (or is mocked with non-ASCII text), [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L24) in `django.core.mail.utils` and [`EmailMessage.message()`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py#L239-L265) in `django.core.mail.message` passed unencoded non-ASCII hostnames into `make_msgid(domain=...)`. When the email was set to a non-Unicode encoding (e.g. `iso-8859-1`), Python attempted to encode the `Message-ID` header using the email charset, which raised a `UnicodeEncodeError`.

### Solution
1. In [`django/core/mail/utils.py`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L24), updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L24) to encode non-ASCII hostnames to ASCII via IDNA (Punycode).
2. In [`django/core/mail/message.py`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py#L257-L270), ensured that the domain passed to `make_msgid(domain=...)` is converted to ASCII via IDNA (Punycode) even when `DNS_NAME` is mocked with a unicode string in tests.
